subject: Order Form clarifications: pricing schedule, min-commit, invoicing sequence
messages:
From: John Doe <john.doe@acme.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acme.com
Date: 2025-09-21T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Clarification on Order Form: invoicing & tax handling

Hi Priya,

Thanks for sending the draft Order Form yesterday. A couple of quick items the procurement and tax teams asked to clarify before we circulate to finance:

- Invoicing cadence: the PDF shows a quarterly invoice but our ERP expects monthly invoices for usage-based charges. Can Redwood issue monthly invoices and a consolidated quarterly statement?
- Taxes: ACME is VAT-registered in the EU and needs a breakdown of VAT vs net charges. Does Redwood present tax line items on invoices or include tax as a separate charge?
- Net terms: procurement prefers Net 45 on the first year to align with our vendor schedule.
- Minimum commit: the commercial schedule shows a 12-month minimum commit; please confirm if we can pro-rate if we terminate early for convenience.

Appreciate a short response so we can move to legal review.

Thanks,
John
John Doe
Senior Procurement Manager
ACME Corporation

--
Attachment: ACME_RFP_summary.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: John Doe <john.doe@acme.com>, ACME Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-09-21T11:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarification on Order Form: invoicing & tax handling

John — thanks for the clear list. I pulled Marcus and Lauren in to confirm commercial/ legal positions. Quick answers up front, then next steps below: 

1) Invoicing cadence: we can issue monthly invoices for usage billing and also provide a consolidated quarterly statement. We'll send the invoice in a machine-readable PDF and include a CSV export in the billing portal.

2) Taxes: Redwood will break out taxes as a separate line item. For EU VAT-registered customers we typically apply net pricing and add VAT per the shipped-to VAT jurisdiction; we can also accept certificate of VAT exemption where applicable.

3) Net terms: Net 30 is our standard for self-serve/hosted, but for committed (reserved) deals we are flexible. Marcus — can you confirm whether Net 45 for Year 1 fits within the finance guardrails?

4) Minimum commit/pro-rate: Our standard Order Form charges the remaining committed amount on termination unless an amendment is agreed. Lauren, can legal provide a limited pro-rate path (e.g., pro-rate for force majeure or mutual termination) or should we leave as-is?

Next steps: Marcus and Lauren will prepare a redline (OrderForm_v3_redline.pdf) and a revised pricing schedule (Redwood_PRICING_SCHEDULE.xlsx). I'll propose a payment/invoice sequence we can attach to the Order Form. If ACME is comfortable with Net 45, we'll include that as an exhibit.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Sr. Account Executive, Redwood Inference
priya_natarajan@redwood.com

--
Attachment: Redwood_PRICING_SCHEDULE.xlsx (pricing spreadsheet stub)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, John Doe <john.doe@acme.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-09-22T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarification on Order Form: invoicing & tax handling

Priya / John — brief finance take:

- Net 45: acceptable for Year 1 with a small credit holdback clause (standard for new enterprise customers). We should note a 1% monthly late fee after 45 days in the Order Form. If ACME requires Net 45 without security, we should add an invoice repayment schedule in the Deal Terms exhibit.
- Monthly invoices + consolidated quarterly statement: fine. Please confirm whether ACME needs invoice-level detail (per-request token counts) or an aggregated usage line. Per-request detail will increase our invoice generation time but is doable.
- Taxes: we will show VAT as a separate line. Accounting needs ACME's VAT ID before first invoice.
- Minimum commit pro-rate: finance prefers a structured early-termination schedule rather than an open pro-rate (e.g., 50% refund of unused committed credits if notice given 60 days prior).

Lauren — can you push the redline to include the holdback and the early-termination schedule? I'll add language to the Deal Terms exhibit for the invoice sequence and late fees.

Marcus Lin
Head of Finance Operations, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com

--
Attachment: Finance_Deal_Exhibit_template.docx (attachment stub)

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: John Doe <john.doe@acme.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-09-23T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Re: Clarification on Order Form: invoicing & tax handling

FYI — attaching the redlined Order Form and a short summary of the changes. Key points we redlined:

- Exhibit A: Pricing schedule updated to include monthly invoice workflow and a sample CSV export file format.
- Section 3 (Payment): Inserted "Net 45 for Year 1" as an option in the payment terms exhibit; included 1% monthly late fee language.
- Section 5 (Taxes): Explicit VAT line item and requirement for customer's VAT ID prior to first invoice.
- Section 7 (Termination): Added structured early-termination credit schedule (60/30/0 days notice tiers) — reduces disputes and preserves revenue predictability.
- Added Deal Terms exhibit with invoice sequence: monthly invoice -> 30-day review window -> payment due Net 45 -> consolidated quarterly statement issuance.

John — please see OrderForm_v3_redline.pdf attached. We can accept edits but prefer not to reopen the MSA unless material. If ACME needs alternative termination economics, we can route to our legal team for negotiation.

Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.com

--
Attachment: OrderForm_v3_redline.pdf (redline PDF stub)

From: John Doe <john.doe@acme.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acme.com
Date: 2025-09-25T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarification on Order Form: invoicing & tax handling

Thanks — we reviewed the redline internally. A few follow-ups:

> From: Lauren Bishop
> Key points we redlined:
> - Inserted "Net 45 for Year 1" as an option
> - 1% monthly late fee
> - VAT line item and VAT ID requirement
> - Early-termination credit schedule

We are comfortable with monthly invoices and VAT line items. A couple of requests before signing:

1) Net 45: ACME can accept Net 45 for Year 1 if the late fee is capped at 0.5% per month instead of 1%.
2) Early-termination: we propose the early-termination schedule be more lenient — 75% refund of unused committed credits with 45 days notice.
3) Invoice detail: Procurement would prefer invoice-level detail aggregated by product line (e.g., Generative tokens, Embeddings calls) rather than raw per-request rows.

If Redwood can accept points 1 and 3, we'll sign the order form and provide the VAT ID in the next 48 hours. We can loop in accounting for a final integration test of invoice CSV format.

Thanks for working through this.

John
Senior Procurement Manager
ACME Corporation

--
Attachment: ACME_VAT_certificate.pdf (pdf stub)
